mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus boosting equity prices and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate indicates a slowing economy, leading to negative equity returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but SPX returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts suggests reduced consumer demand, leading to negative equity returns as economic growth falters.
failure_condition: If HOUST drops but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment combined with slowing payroll growth indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS growth slows but SPX returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply chain issues, leading to negative equity returns as corporate earnings are impacted.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, suppressing equity valuations and leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains high but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending suggests strong demand, boosting corporate revenues and leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: If RSAFS grows but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth combined with rising inflation indicates stagflation, leading to negative equity returns as growth falters and costs rise.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL rises but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
